draft.title: Postulates of special relativity
card: An inertial frame is a frame of reference that moves at constant velocity, with no acceleration. A lab at rest and a train gliding at steady speed are both inertial frames.
the laws of physics are the same in every inertial frame. No experiment done inside a frame can show whether that frame is at rest or moving at steady speed.
the speed of light in a vacuum, c, is the same for all observers. It does not depend on how fast the source or the observer is moving.
The second postulate breaks the everyday rule of adding speeds. If a torch is switched on in a fast spaceship, observers in the ship and outside both measure light moving at c.
draft.remember: Same laws in every inertial frame, and the same value of c for every observer.

a.q: A spaceship moves past Earth at a steady, very high speed. It fires a pulse of light forwards. What do observers on Earth measure for the speed of the pulse in a vacuum?
opts: c, the same as the crew on the ship measure
c plus the speed of the spaceship
c minus the speed of the spaceship
Less than c, because the ship is moving
a.why: The speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers, whatever the motion of the source. Adding the ship's speed to c is the everyday rule, and the second postulate rules it out.
a.clue: Does the speed of the source change the speed of light?

b.q: Priya is on a train moving at a steady speed. She does a physics experiment in a closed carriage with no windows. Which statement follows from the first postulate?
opts: The experiment cannot show if the train is moving steadily
The experiment gives different laws from the platform's
The experiment can measure the train's steady speed
The experiment works only if the train is at rest
b.why: The laws of physics are the same in every inertial frame, so no experiment inside the carriage can tell steady motion from rest. The claim that the laws differ on the platform is the tempting mistake, and the first postulate rules it out.
b.clue: A train at steady speed is an inertial frame.

a.best: c, the same as the crew on the ship measure

b.best: The experiment cannot show if the train is moving steadily
